title: Why the heart is called lev: thirty-two paths from the mind, and the will felt even in the breath
overview: Chapter 32 brings the end of the world of the *Ein Sof* down to the outer vessels of *Zeir Anpin*, the "upper man" on the throne, and explains it from man. In the soul, the will and delight of *yechida* are beyond any vessel, yet they shine, hidden, into the brain and from it into the heart; the heart's love and hate are themselves a will. The will reaches the heart along the 32 paths: *daas* opens into the brains of *chesed* and *gevura*, four brains of eight rooms each, and that is why the heart is called *lev*. The fifty gates of *bina* are doors, still hidden in the mind; the 32 paths are roads, the arousal already on its way through *daas*. Before the mind's love becomes the heart's there is a withdrawal at the narrow of the throat, a change of essence, yet the heart's *middos* match the mind's exactly. And the essential will is felt even in the breath of the heart, as one thing. The classes turn the grid of brains into how one should think, and into a digression on the sixty-four brains of one who contemplates, whose mind is on fire.

terms.gloss: the world of the Infinite; here brought down to the outer vessels of Zeir Anpin
the level of the soul above the vessels with yechida; the source of intellect, the maskil

paths, roadways: the 32 paths as they are called in chachma

a change of essence: intellect becoming an actual midda of the heart

sections.title: Zeir Anpin, the man on the throne, is still the end of the world of the Ein Sof
sections.summary: The "upper man" on the throne is *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus*, the *middos*, the root of the flow that gives life to the worlds. Even its vessels, down to the outer *Nehi*, still count as the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*.

phrases.he: (לב) ומעתה יש להבין בבחינת אדם העליון דאצילות שעל הכסא כו'
שהוא בחינת זעיר אנפין דאצילות שמקבל מבחינת נה''י דאבא ואמא כו'
וידוע שהוא ענין ובחינת המדות דאצילות,
שהוא עיקר ושרש להשפעת מקור למקור לחיי העולמות
phrases.en: That's really the creator of the world.

blocks.text: The chapter turns to the "upper man" of *Atzilus* who sits on the throne: *Zeir Anpin* (lit. the small countenance) of *Atzilus*, which receives from the *Nehi* of *Abba* and *Ima*. It is the *middos* of *Atzilus*, the root of the flow that gives life to the worlds: **That's really the creator of the world**. In many places, when they say G-d, this is what they are talking about: *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus*, the man who sits on the chair.

phrases.he: ועדיין הוא סוף עולם האין סוף,
phrases.en: And really this is also still considered the end of the *olam ha'Ein Sof*.

phrases.he: משום דאיהו וחיוהי וגרמוהי חד
כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: In the last chapter.

phrases.he: על כן גם עד בחינת כלים דזעיר אנפין בבחינת חיצוניות דנה''י שבו כו', נחשב עדיין מסוף עולם האין סוף:

blocks.text: This is **still considered the end of the *olam ha'Ein Sof*** (the world of the Infinite). Before, it reached only to the inner *Atik*, then *Arich*; now, to the vessels of *Zeir Anpin*, which is still called G-d, the Holy One, blessed be He: "He and His life and His causes are one." The vessels of *Zeir Anpin* are *mamash* (literally) the *gufa d'malka* (the body of the King), as in "to bow to the body of the King"

sections.title: In man: the will above all vessels shines, hidden, into the brain and the heart
sections.summary: In the soul, *chaya* and *yechida* encompass and are not limited in any vessel; only from *chachma* down is there a vessel. Yet the will and delight shine, hidden, into the brain and from it into the heart, and the *middos* of the heart are themselves a will.

phrases.he: וביאור הדברים, הנה מבשרי אחזה כו', דבצלם אלהי״ם עשה את האדם כו', וכמו שכתוב בצלמינו כדמותינו כו'
דהנה אנו רואים בנפש האדם שבחינת חיה יחידה שבו, הוא בחינת מקיפין דנר''ן, שלמעלה מהגבלת האורות בכלים
והוא בחינת הרצון והתענוג העצמי הפשוט שבבחינת יחידה, וגם בחינת פנימית ומקור השכל שנקרא משכיל, שזהו בחינת מקיף דחיה
בלתי מוגבלים בכלי כלל
רק מהחכמה ולמטה נמשך בכלי
והוא הנשמה שבמוחא, ורוח בלב כו'

blocks.text:
"From my flesh I see G-d": man is in the image of G-d. In the soul, *chaya* and *yechida* are the *makifim* (encompassing levels), above being limited in vessels: the essential will and delight of *yechida*, and the source of intellect, the *maskil*, of *chaya*. Only from *chachma* down is there a vessel: the *neshama* in the brain, the *ruach* in the heart.

The inner *chachma* is unlimited, and by the way, so is the inner *bina*: some places say *chachma* and *bina* together are called *chachma*, and *Yisroel Saba* and *tevuna* are called *bina*. So the inner *bina* is up there too.

phrases.he: והנה עם כל זה מאיר אור המקיף דרצון ותענוג, מבחינת פנימית אור החכמה בנר''ן שבג' כלים מוחא ולבא כו',
phrases.en: You see that the *ratzon* is *meir* in them, even though it's not *mugbal* by them.

phrases.he: מן ההעלם
phrases.en: In a hidden way.

phrases.he: והוא גלוי הרצון שבא בשכל וטעם גלוי, בבחינת מוח החכמה שנקרא אור אבא
phrases.en: That's where the *sechel* already comes in a *taam galui*.

phrases.he: ומשם נמשך ומתפשט בבינה, שהוא ההשגה
ומבינה שבמוח נמשך התפעלות המדות בלב

blocks.text: Even so, the encompassing light of will and delight shines into the three vessels, brain and heart: the *ratzon* (will) **is *meir* in them, even though it's not *mugbal* by them**, in **a hidden way**. It is revealed in the mind of *chachma*, called *Abba*, where **the *sechel* already comes in a *taam galui*** (a revealed reason). From there it spreads into *bina*, the grasp, and from *bina* in the mind comes the arousal of the *middos* in the heart.
The *middos* of the heart are really a will. What is love? A will for something. And hate? A will against something. As it says, *ahava* (love) is *ava*, "he wants", with a *hei* in it.

sections.title: Thirty-two paths: four brains of eight rooms, tilting toward chesed or gevura
sections.summary: From *bina* the will travels to the heart along the 32 *shvilin* (paths). *Daas* opens into two brains, *chesed* and *gevura*, making four, each with eight rooms; the 32 rooms are why the heart is called *lev*. Every thought is placed by direction: front or back, up or down, right or left.

phrases.he: דהיינו מל''ב חדרים שבמוח שנקרא ל''ב שבילין דבינה
דמתפתחין להיות מוחין לזעיר אנפין כו'
phrases.en: They travel all the way down to *Zeir Anpin*.

blocks.text: From the 32 rooms in the brain called the 32 *shvilin* (paths) of *bina*. Elsewhere they are the 32 *netivos* (paths) of *chachma*; here he calls them *shvilin* of *bina*, and he is talking about the inner *bina*.

blocks.question: Is this because, as in *Derech Chaim*, there are two sets of 32 paths: one from *chachma* to *bina*, the *shvilin*, and one drawn from *Arich* into *chachma*?
blocks.text: It is the same one. As learned before, where it comes from in *Arich* is where it is in *chachma*: from the *mazalos*, in the *Chabad* of *Chabad*; from the *middos*, in the *middos* of *Chabad*. And, as the student said, it doubles over into 64. When he says the 32 *shvilin* of *bina* it is the inner *bina*, which is in *Arich*.

blocks.title: Route 66
blocks.text: That is why they are called *shvilin*: a *shvil*, like a *nesiv*, is a road, and a road goes from one place to another, like Route 66 in the song, through St. Louis, down to Missouri, down to Oklahoma. These 32 paths go from the inside out and from the outside in; you can travel them both ways. **They travel all the way down to *Zeir Anpin***, which is why it is called a *lev* (heart): that is where the paths are going.
Now he is going to explain the 32 *shvilin* of *bina*. By the way, this is chapter 32, *lamed-beis*, and that is also what *lev* is.

phrases.he: כי המוחין נחלקים לד', חכמה ובינה וחסד וגבורה
phrases.en: Because the *mochin* open up into four: *chachma*, *bina*, *chesed* and *gevura*.

phrases.he: וכל אחד יש בו ח' חדרים,
phrases.en: Each one of these brains has eight rooms in it.

phrases.he: שהוא ל''ב

blocks.text: For **the *mochin* open up into four**: *daas* opens into two brains, since *daas* is the *memutza* (mediator) between *chesed* and *gevura*. These *chesed* and *gevura* are not *middos*; they are *mamash* brains. So instead of three brains there are four.

blocks.title: The cerebellum, a double brain
blocks.text: He sent this once to a doctor he learns with, and she said: the cerebellum is a double brain. As the front brain is made of two sides, the cerebellum looks like one brain but is really two brains back there, and they are not really sure how it works. He does not know the particulars, but here it says how it works: it opens up into the two brains of *chesed* and *gevura*.

**Each one of these brains has eight rooms in it**, eight *chadarim*, which makes 32: a front brain and a back brain. He does not know whether it is said here or he learned it elsewhere, but the eight rooms are the interweaving of *Havaya* and *Adnus*. And this is the whole matter of the *sukka*: it has eight *sukkos* in it.

blocks.title: The square with a sukka on each corner
blocks.text: *Chachma*, *bina*, *chesed* and *gevura* make a square, not a cube. On each corner of the square is a cube, which is eight: a *sukka* on each one of them. This whole square is the ceiling of the *sukka*, and the heart is its floor, another square with another eight rooms. That is why it is called *lev*.

blocks.title: The matrix: tic-tac-toe and the computer screen
blocks.text: And if you look at this, it is a matrix. What is a matrix? A tic-tac-toe.

blocks.title: The matrix: tic-tac-toe and the computer screen
blocks.text: A tic-tac-toe is a matrix three by three; this one is a strange matrix, with a big square and little squares, where usually all the squares are the same. A matrix is like a tax table, or bingo's B28, or the chess board, where the rook moves along the length and the width. A computer screen works as a matrix: the program tells it position 1,1 is green, position 1,2 is green. Really it is simpler, only on and off; it cannot say red or blue. There are three colors: position 1,1 is red, position 1,2 is blue, and the third he does not remember. A student once wrote a whole piece on the colors.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 048 opens by finishing the matrix begun at the end of class 047, before it reads the chapter again from line 1.

phrases.he: והיינו הטעם שנקרא לב, מפני ששרשו בל''ב שבילין, הן ל''ב חדרים
שעל ידם דעת, שכולל חסד וגבורה, מטה אור השכל דחכמה ובינה להתפעלות לחסד וגבורה, כלפי זכות או כלפי חוב
phrases.en: So the *daas* is *mateh* it towards these two brains of *chesed* and *gevura*, and they actually *hispaalus*.

blocks.text: That is why the heart is called *lev*: its root is in the 32 *shvilin*, the 32 rooms. Through them *daas*, which includes *chesed* and *gevura*, tilts the light of the intellect of *chachma* and *bina* toward arousal, **towards these two brains of *chesed* and *gevura***, toward merit or toward guilt.

blocks.title: Jackie Mason's finger
blocks.text: This is also why Talmudic logic works the way it does. You know Jackie Mason with the finger: to the right and to the left, and down and up, like a circle. So there is right and left, front and back, and down and up, which is the descent of *yud-kei-vav-kei*: those are the rooms.

In general there are two in the front and two in the back. In thinking, the front is intellect and the back is *middos*: is it an intellect of intellect, or an intellect of *middos*? And it goes up and down: up toward *Havaya*, toward *Elokus*, or down toward the world, even when it is pure intellect. So the *Chassidus* we are learning now is *davka* (precisely) intellect going up, and the *iyun* (close analysis) of the Talmud is *davka* intellect going down.

Within that there is a front and a back, and also a right and a left: in the back *chesed* and *gevura*, in the front *chachma* and *bina*, the spreading out of the whole or the contracting of the particulars, holistic intellect or "logistic" intellect. Each can go up or down. The back too can be an emotion of spreading out, and it too goes up or down: an intellect of emotions need not have to do with emotions going down; it can belong above intellect altogether. Intellect going up goes above intellect; intellect going down goes below it.

Up to now the whole intellect is up; within it are four intellects, and they go up and down: in each, a *chachma*, *bina*, *chesed* and *gevura* going up and a *chachma*, *bina*, *chesed* and *gevura* going down. That is eight. And each of these eight points has a room on it, and a room is a cube: on each point there is one more whole thing like that. It keeps going, but he speaks of eight main rooms, and in each room eight points, like a *sukka*.

blocks.title: The man in the sukka
blocks.text: These eight points include everything. As we said of the *sukka*, the man inside it does the *naanuim* (the shakings of the lulav), and the *naanuim* are seven *middos*. Seven *middos* each of seven are 49, the *nun shaarei bina* (the fifty gates of *bina*). So the fifty gates and the 32 paths are the same thing in different ways, and they include each other. And this whole thing is really going up: even the parts going down are part of the going up, because it is all in the brain.

sections.title: Fifty gates and thirty-two paths: the brain in bina and the brain in daas
sections.summary: The *middos* within the intellect, seven times seven, are the fifty gates of *bina*: doors, still hidden in the grasp. The 32 paths are roads: the beginning of the arousal travelling, through *daas*, from the mind into the heart. That is why the heart is called *lev*.

phrases.he: ונקרא גם כן מדות שבשכל, שהן בחינת ז׳ תחתונים דבינה, וכל אחד כלול מז',
phrases.en: So the *chesed* and *gevura* going back is also called the *middos* of the *sechel* of *bina*, which is *chesed* and *gevura*; it includes the whole *middos*, and each one is made up from seven.

phrases.he: שהן נ׳ שערי בינה
והכל ענין אחד,
phrases.en: It's all one thing.

phrases.he: רק שנ׳ שערי בינה הוא עדיין בהשגה דבינה, כמו חסדים המכוסים תוך יסוד אימא כו'

blocks.text: So **the *chesed* and *gevura* going back is also called the *middos* of the *sechel* of *bina***, the seven lower ones of *bina*, each made up of seven: the fifty gates. **It's all one thing**, only the fifty gates are still in the grasp of *bina*, hidden like the kindnesses covered inside the *yesod* of *Ima*. It is before you even think: in the *Darkei Moshe*, say, the 32 paths are already going toward the *pilpul* that comes out of it; the fifty gates are how it was even before that.

phrases.he: היינו בחינת התפעלות האהבה שבשכל והשגה עדיין, שנקרא מכוסה ונעלם בהשגה
phrases.en: It's really still completely hidden inside the *sechel*.

phrases.he: ואחר כך יוצא לגילוי מהות התפעלות מדת אהבה שבלב, שנקרא זעיר אנפין

blocks.text: This is the arousal of love still in the intellect and the grasp. **It's really still completely hidden inside the *sechel***. Afterwards it comes out into the revealed arousal of love in the heart, *Zeir Anpin*, and in the same way the 32 *shvilin* come out from the hidden arousal in the mind to the heart. That is what *shvilin* are: the paths from the mind to the heart. The fifty gates have a different name.

blocks.title: A door, not a wall
blocks.text: A *shaar* (gate) is a door. Something can come out of it, but nothing necessarily is coming out. The door is not going anywhere; it is part of the house, an opening through which something can come out. That is why the hidden *middos* of *bina* are called gates: something can come out of them. A wall lets nothing out; a gate can.

Another meaning of *shaar* is *shiur*, a measure: the measure in the mind of what the *midda* will be. It is not an actual *midda*; as a listener said, it is in the hiddenness of the intellect. It is only a measure in *bina*, worked out logically, like: if you had a brother, would he like cheese? Just logic, not an actual *midda* at all.

With the 32 *netivos* it is different. Their front is *chachma* and *bina*, but it is a square, connected to its back, the brain of *daas*: the whole brain works connected to *daas*. So it is already the actual beginning of the actual arousal that is going to go down into the heart. That is why it is called a *nesiv*, a roadway: a roadway actually travels from one place to another.

blocks.title: Jackie Mason's thumb and the breakdancer
blocks.text: And that is how you think. Like Jackie Mason's thumb: not this point, and this point, and this point, but a flow. A mime, or the breakdancing, is not a flow: this point and then that point, a jerk. Those are points, each one in its place, and a gate is like that: something can come out of it. A path is like Jackie Mason's thumb, a movement from one place to another: up to down, down to up, or side to side, "on the other hand", from the right to the left, *chesed* one way and *gevura* the other.

This is really the matter of *daas*, while the fifty gates are mainly *bina*, how the brain is in *bina*. *Chachma* and *bina* are two companions that never part: there is no *chachma* without *bina*. And it says: if there is no *daas* there is no *bina*, and if there is no *bina* there is no *daas*. You cannot explain something to someone who will not listen and have him understand, and you cannot come up with an explanation when you do not know what you are talking about at all. Without an explanation there will be no knowledge.

You are not going to just sit and concentrate and have knowledge come. A *daas* that brings knowledge automatically, by itself, just because you are concentrating, cannot be: that is the whole business of *goyishkeit* (the non-Jewish way). There is no *bina*, there is no *daas*.

sensitivity.reason: Calls knowledge sought by concentration alone, without understanding, the way of goyishkeit.
sensitivity.publishable: You are not going to just sit and concentrate and have knowledge come. A *daas* that brings knowledge automatically, by itself, just because you are concentrating, cannot be. There is no *bina*, there is no *daas*.

blocks.text: They all work together, but there is how the intellect is in *bina*, and in *chachma*, the front, and how it is in *daas*, the actual *hataya* (inclination) of the intellect toward the actual thing. As he said in chapter 2, the *middos* come out of *tevuna*; but *tevuna* is a kind of *bina*, and even from *tevuna* nothing would come out without *daas*. Coming out to something outside itself is *davka* through *tevuna*, but the actual coming down into the *middos* is from *daas*. Why, then, say it is from *bina* or *tevuna*? Because *daas* is basically the *middos*: the brain of the *middos*, *chesed* and *gevura*, but a brain, not yet a *midda*. So the fifty gates are how the brain is in *bina*, and the 32 paths are how the brain is in *daas*, including *chachma* and *bina*.

phrases.he: ועל דרך זה יוצאים ל''ב שבילין הנזכר לעיל בהתגלות מן התפעלות ההעלם שבמוח ללב,
ועל כן נקרא לב
phrases.en: That's why it's called a *lev*.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים בטעם שנקרא לב, מפני שמתקבצים שם ל''ב אורות דאבא ואמא, שהן ל''ב שבילין
(והן ל''ב ויאמר אלהי״ם דבינה שמקבל מאבא)
phrases.en: I think it says the 32 *Vayomer Elokim* in the creation of the world, which receives from *Abba*.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות.

blocks.text: In this way the 32 *shvilin* come out, revealed, from the hidden arousal in the mind to the heart. **That's why it's called a *lev***. Why should the heart be named for 32 paths in the brain? Because the fifty gates are the brain as a brain, and the *lev* is how it comes into the heart: it is the *daas*, the brain as it comes into the heart, the actual arousal of what is going to come out into the heart.

So the *Etz Chaim* explains that it is called *lev* because the 32 lights of *Abba* and *Ima*, the 32 *shvilin*, gather there. He thinks these are the 32 times "And G-d said" in the creation of the world, which receive from *Abba*, and that is why they are sometimes called the 32 *netivos* of *chachma*: in *chachma* they are called *netivos*, and in *bina* the 32 *shvilin* of *bina*.

Before going on to a new matter he goes over this in terms of how you think, and how the whole of reality is grasped by the brain, since the brain is what sees a world out there. First, in anything that comes up, your brain has to decide immediately: forward or back? Is it a logical thing, *sechel'dik*, or an emotive thing?

blocks.title: Did he bring flowers?
blocks.text: When your wife gets mad at you and has a reason, what do you do? An illogical person just shouts back. A logical person, with forebrains, first asks: is it really the logical reason that bothers her, or is it covering up something emotive, and really I did not bring her flowers for a while? And notice: at this point, not bringing flowers is not an emotion. It is an analysis, pure intellect, an intellect of an emotion.

sensitivity.reason: A husband-and-wife example in which the wife's stated reason covers up an emotional complaint.
sensitivity.publishable: When someone close to you gets mad at you and has a reason, what do you do? An illogical person just shouts back. A logical person, with forebrains, first asks: is it really the logical reason that bothers them, or is it covering up something emotive, and really I did not bring flowers for a while? And notice: at this point, not bringing flowers is not an emotion. It is an analysis, pure intellect, an intellect of an emotion.

blocks.text: So the first thing to decide in anything is: does it go forward or back? Then: right or left? Once you do that, it is placed on one of the four points of the square of your brain: if it goes forward, it is *chachma* or *bina*; if it goes back, it is a matter of *chesed* or of *gevura*.

Within each of those are eight rooms: two forward and two back, and on top of them another two forward and two back. So again: within this, is it a matter of intellect or of emotion? And up or down: once you place it in *chachma*, is it *chachma* going up or *chachma* going down? Within *chachma* going up, is it *chachma*, *bina*, *chesed* or *gevura*? The *middos* of *Atik*, for example, are *chachma* going up, intellect going up: contemplating the *middos* of *Atik* has nothing to do with emotions, it is pure *hisbonenus* (contemplation), and yet within that contemplation there can also be *middos*.

It goes down, then to the left and up: all kinds of combinations, as they say of the brain, the synapses going from this one to that one. Within each of the four points are eight rooms, and that is as far as he goes. But a room has eight points and six directions, so already there are seven *middos* there. And these are all intellects.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 049 opens by finishing the grid of the four brains and their rooms from the end of class 048, before it reads line 28.

blocks.title: The TV screen: a grid of on and off
blocks.text: What we have is a grid. Represent physical reality in two dimensions and you get a computer screen or a TV screen, and all a TV screen is, is yes, no, no, yes, yes. On the screen a point cannot change colors; it can only go on and off, and the colors come from clusters of three points, red, blue and yellow (he is not sure those are the three). But here it is a bunch of rooms: each point is not just a point but a whole room.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 049 opens by finishing the grid of the four brains and their rooms from the end of class 048, before it reads line 28.

blocks.title: The little Aibershter with a lulav
blocks.text: Inside each room is a little guy, a little *Aibershter* (the One Above, G-d) standing there with a lulav, who can change the color into the seven colors of the rainbow, since each *sefira* has a color. There are only six *naanuim*, but they include seven *sefiros*: the seventh is when he brings it in to himself. Right is *chesed*, left is *gevura*, forward is *tiferes*, up is *netzach*, down is *hod*, back is *Malchus*, toward the west, and he himself, the lulav, is *yesod*, "the *tzaddik* is the foundation of the world". "For all that is in heaven and earth": he connects heaven and earth and all four directions. And it is three-dimensional, with zillions and trillions and quadrillions of these little guys.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 049 opens by finishing the grid of the four brains and their rooms from the end of class 048, before it reads line 28.

blocks.title: The cathode gun: one point at a time
blocks.text: But really it is not like that: there is really only one guy. On a TV there is really only one point. A cathode gun shoots out light at a point, basically like a *tzimtzum* and a *Kav*, and moves across, one point at a time. So how could the whole world exist? On a TV there is a lag: the point glows a little after the light hits it, and the gun moves fast. Does that mean a point glows a little even after the *Aibershter* is no longer there? No: He moves so fast that He is in all the places at the same time.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 049 opens by finishing the grid of the four brains and their rooms from the end of class 048, before it reads line 28.

blocks.text: It says here that *yesod* is west and *Malchus* the holy sanctuary in the middle. That is not the usual way: usually *Malchus* is west, and the whole creation bows to the west because *Malchus* is there. Saying it the other way is "Your kingship is the kingship of all worlds": *Malchus* is called a *dalet* because it spreads out to the four directions and through all the worlds. But it makes no difference; *yesod* and *Malchus* are sort of interchangeable, depending how you want to look at it, so you can say either is in the west.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 049 opens by finishing the grid of the four brains and their rooms from the end of class 048, before it reads line 28.

blocks.text: The usual thing, in most places, is that *Malchus* is in the west, which is why the *Beis HaMikdash* went toward the west, and the little guy standing in the *sukka* is *yesod*, "the *tzaddik* is the foundation of the world". "For all that is in heaven and earth": *yesod* makes the connections between the directions, from heaven to earth, right to left and forward to back, since *shamayim* (heaven) is fire and water, and earth is *Malchus*. That is why he is called *kol*, all: he can make you any color you want. And *Malchus* can have everything too: the final point that comes out on the screen. It has nothing of its own, only what *yesod* told it to be: green, then green; blue, then blue.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 049 opens by finishing the grid of the four brains and their rooms from the end of class 048, before it reads line 28.

blocks.text: That is the grid, and that is the way your brain thinks: in directions. The physical directions come out of the emotional directions, which come out of the intellectual directions, which come from directions higher up, all from the *Kav*. The grid in your mind goes into your heart too. Sit back and you feel you have a head, a heart and a bottom: that is your feeling of up and down. Mainly it is a head and a heart, since the guts, the *Nehi*, are included in the *Chagas*. Up and down means the up of the brain coming down into the heart.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 049 opens by finishing the grid of the four brains and their rooms from the end of class 048, before it reads line 28.

blocks.title: Sixty-four brains
blocks.text: He thinks a later chapter explains that this is also the matter of the *tzaddik*, and it comes *davka* through contemplation, which opens *daas* into two brains. In an ordinary person *daas* is one brain: emotion. With no *hisbonenus*, no analysis, it is just arousal, like an animal's, which is why it says one who does not contemplate is an animal: he has three brains and that is all. In one who contemplates, *daas* opens into two, so he has four brains, and automatically 32. Then the 32 paths go down into the heart and become another 32 there, brains, not *middos*: sixty-four brains, more than twenty times the brainpower of an ordinary person. And that is only quantity.
blocks.outOfPlace: After reading line 28, class 049 stops the text and goes back to the 32 paths that go down into the heart: the sixty-four brains of one who contemplates.

blocks.title: Brains on fire, a cold heart
blocks.text: Then quality: the brains in his brain become hot and his heart becomes cold. A cold-hearted person, like the song, "your cold, cold heart"? No: his *middos* do not boil over; they follow the intellect. But his intellect is no longer a cold, logical brain; it is a fire. So it is not thirty times more but beyond comparison. Light does not just come into his brain from somewhere else; he is a *maor* (a source of light), a fire, because it is *daas*: he is totally connected, totally interested. Even a little real *daas* is beyond comparison with ordinary thinking, and he has 64 brains on fire. The 32 brains in his heart are on fire too, so really his heart is on fire, and the light of a brain is much more than the light of a heart. Only the outer, emotional heart is cold, so the emotions cannot interfere. Usually the emotions are on fire and the brain is cold; by him the brain is on fire.
blocks.outOfPlace: After reading line 28, class 049 stops the text and goes back to the 32 paths that go down into the heart: the sixty-four brains of one who contemplates.

blocks.text: This is the actual arousal, and it comes only through contemplation. Not what other people think: this is the real arousal we are going for, the inner kind rather than the outer. The outer arousal, the crying and the like, is also something, but it is nothing compared to this. The real arousal is when he becomes all the way, with sixty-four brains.
blocks.outOfPlace: After reading line 28, class 049 stops the text and goes back to the 32 paths that go down into the heart: the sixty-four brains of one who contemplates.

blocks.title: The sixty-fourth brain
blocks.text: It says a *talmid chacham* (Torah scholar) with more than a sixty-fourth of *ga'ava* (pride) is a *gas ruach* (coarse of spirit). *Gas* is sixty-three: he has only 63 brains, so really only three, and only thinks he has 64. But it also means the other way: lacking that sixty-fourth of pride shows he is a *gas ruach*, without the sixty-fourth brain, the main brain of *Chassidus*, pride with *Chassidus*: "let him who glories glory in this", "his heart was lifted up in the ways of G-d".
blocks.outOfPlace: After reading line 28, class 049 stops the text and goes back to the 32 paths that go down into the heart: the sixty-four brains of one who contemplates.

blocks.text: When it comes to an attack on *Chassidus*, on G-dliness, on *Yiddishkeit*, on the *Rebbe*, all of a sudden he is not five cents anymore. He turns into a werewolf: super haughty, he will totally knock the other guy down. And that is actually the sign of humility, which most people do not understand. Go against the *Aibershter*, and it is a whole different story. About himself he is very humble, but about Reform and Conservative there is nothing to talk about with him: "These people are not rabbis, and only I'm right." Totally arrogant, it seems; but *davka* the one who does not get fired up at an affront to the *Aibershter* shows he is a *gas ruach*, without the sixty-fourth brain.
blocks.outOfPlace: After reading line 28, class 049 stops the text and goes back to the 32 paths that go down into the heart: the sixty-four brains of one who contemplates.

blocks.title: Matisyahu and Mordechai
blocks.text: How can you say such a thing? Look through history. Matisyahu was a humble little old man, "Oh, hello, how are you?" Then it came to that, and he took a sword and killed the goy and the Jew in front of everybody, without a word. Mordechai, the *Rebbe*, was very humble; but when Haman came up as an affront to the *Aibershter*, "he would not bend or bow". The Jews told him he would make Haman mad; he said, "I don't care." And Matisyahu says, "Everybody who is for the..." (the tape ends).
blocks.outOfPlace: After reading line 28, class 049 stops the text and goes back to the 32 paths that go down into the heart: the sixty-four brains of one who contemplates.

sections.title: The narrow of the throat: a withdrawal before the mind's love becomes the heart's
sections.summary: For the *midda* in the mind to become a *midda* in the heart there must first be a contraction and withdrawal, like a seed that rots before it grows: the narrow of the throat of *bina*, like the membrane between the source of intellect and intellect, and the liver between the organs of breath and of food.

phrases.he: והנה ודאי כאשר צריך להיות התהוות התפעלות המדה בלב מן העלם התפעלות המדה בהיותה בשכל והשגה דבינה, הוצרך להיות תחלה בחינת צמצום והעלם וכיווץ שנקרא הסתלקות (כמו משל רקבון הגרעין בשביל השתנות ממהות למהות וכידוע)
והוא בחינת מיצר הגרון דבינה,
phrases.en: This is the *tzimtzum* between the brain and the heart, which is the throat, called the narrowness of the throat.

phrases.he: שנתעלם שם התפעלות השכל ונמשך להיות בשינוי המהות בהתפעלות הלב
(וכמו בחינת קרומא כו'
phrases.en: Which is between the *maskil* and the *sechel*.

phrases.he: שהוא המעלים ומפסיק מכח עליון שלמעלה מן השכל, לבוא לשינוי המהות בגלוי אור השכלה כו'
וכמו חצר הכבד
phrases.en: And then on a lower level is another place where the next *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: שמפסיק ומבדיל בין אברי הנשימה לאברי המזון להיות שינוי המהות וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות)

blocks.text: When the arousal of the *midda* in the heart has to come out of its hidden arousal in the intellect and grasp of *bina*, there must first be a *tzimtzum* (contraction), a hiding and a withdrawal, as in the example of the seed that rots in order to change from one thing into another. That is the *meitzar hagaron* (the narrow of the throat) of *bina*: **the *tzimtzum* between the brain and the heart**, where the arousal of the intellect is hidden and drawn out as a *shinui hamahus* (a change of essence), the arousal of the heart. It is like the *kruma* (membrane), **between the *maskil* and the *sechel***, which hides and separates the power above intellect so that it can come to a change of essence in revealed intellect.

blocks.question: Is the separation he means the diaphragm?
blocks.text: No. Below the throat is another place of the next *tzimtzum*, the *chatzar hakaved* (lit. the court of the liver), which separates the organs of breathing from the organs of food. The diaphragm is not it: it is just the physical border, the end of the lungs, the thing that pushes the lungs in and out, and nothing passes through it. Where it goes over from one to the other there is a transformation, a change of essence, and that is in the liver, which is basically a filter.

sections.title: The heart's middos match the mind's exactly, and even their outer vessels are still Ein Sof
sections.summary: The *middos* in the heart come out exactly as they were in the mind, only changed in essence and limited by *netzach* and *hod* of *bina*, the "therefore" of the reasoning. Each has three levels and three vessels; even the outermost, the breath of the chest, is still the *Ein Sof*.

phrases.he: אך עם כל זה המדות שבלב הן בדומה ממש אל המדות שבשכל, ממש כאופני התפעלותם במוח,
phrases.en: Exactly how you think in the brain.

phrases.he: בלי נטיה כקוצו של יו''ד כידוע
רק שבלב באין בשינוי המהות ובהגבלה וצמצום דבחינת נצח והוד דבינה, שהוא שליחות שפע אור ההשגה בעצם,
בשביל התפעלות המדה לבד כידוע
phrases.en: It's not the *etzem*, it's only the *shlichus* for the *hispaalus hamidda levad*.

blocks.text: Even so, the heart's *middos* are exactly like the mind's: **Exactly how you think in the brain**. In the brain it is intellect and in the heart an actual *midda*, a change of essence; yet they come out exactly as in *bina*. Understand that someone is doing you good, and the love in your heart is as big as the love in your brain, without a deviation of the tip of a *yud*.

Only in the heart they come with a change of essence, limited and contracted by the *netzach* and *hod* of *bina*, the sending of the grasp for the arousal of the *midda*. That is what is called the *uvchein* ("and so"): so, therefore, I like the guy.

blocks.question: What does *b'etzem* mean here?
blocks.text: The essence of the grasp itself, in *bina*. *Netzach* and *hod* are only the *shlichus* (sending) of that essence, not the essence: **it's only the *shlichus* for the *hispaalus hamidda levad***, for the arousal of the *midda* alone. It is only the *uvchein*: so, therefore, I like the guy. It is only the "therefore" of the intellect.

phrases.he: ובמדות שבלב כלול מג' מדריגות, חב''ד חג''ת נה''י
דהיינו בחינת המושכל ומורגש ומוטבע
הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: Same like we said before.

phrases.he: וג' כלים לכל אחד, פנימית ואמצעית וחיצוניות
phrases.en: And each one of them has three *kelim*.

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל באריכות
phrases.en: This was all discussed earlier.

blocks.text: The *middos* in the heart include three levels, *Chabad*, *Chagas* and *Nehi*: the *muskal* (the understood), the *murgash* (the felt) and the *mutba* (the instinctive), the **same like we said before**. And **each one of them has three *kelim***, inner, middle and outer.

phrases.he: אך הנה גם בחינת החיצוניות דכלים דנה''י שבלב - שהוא בחינת התפעלות החסד והאהבה שבלב כשבאה לידי השפעה לחוץ,
שנקרא נה''י דחזה
phrases.en: The lungs: the lungs are the external of the heart.

phrases.he: במחשבה דיבור ומעשה,
היינו על ידי חיצוניות הכלי דלב, שהוא בחינת המוטבע אשר בהבל החזה דזעיר אנפין דאצילות,
phrases.en: The *mutba* in the *chaze*: meaning that according to the *teva*, when you get upset, you start breathing hard.

phrases.he: שעל זה אמר איהו וגרמוהי חד
- הכל עדיין בבחינת אין סוף
phrases.en: Even down to there: even the fact that your lungs are breathing hard, it's still you, completely connected to you.

blocks.text: Even the outer vessels of the heart's *Nehi*, its love coming outward in thought, speech and action, come through the outer vessel of the heart: the *mutba* in the breath of the chest, the lungs. **The lungs are the external of the heart.** By nature, when you get upset you start breathing hard. That is neither *muskal* nor even *murgash*, not the feeling of love or hate or that I like this guy. The *muskal* is still an *uvchein*, the final "therefore"; here it is a *mutba*.

blocks.title: The bull breathing fire
blocks.text: That is the breathing of the heart, like the bull that starts breathing fire: that is the *mutba*, the *Nehi* in the breath of the chest. That is why anger is called *charon af* (lit. the burning of the nose): when he gets mad, he is breathing hard.

This is the *mutba* in the breath of the chest of *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus*, of which it says, "He and His causes are one": even down to there, it is all still the *Ein Sof*. In a person, **even the fact that your lungs are breathing hard, it's still you**, completely connected to you.

sections.title: The essential will is felt in the breath of the heart, and so in Zeir Anpin: it is, and it isn't
sections.summary: In a person the essential will, after all its contractions, is felt even in the breath of the heart, as one thing with its source. So in *Zeir Anpin*: the simple will from before the first *tzimtzum* shines in the outer vessels of its heart, still the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*. Is it the Essence? It is and it isn't.

phrases.he: וכמו על דרך משל באדם התחתון כאשר הרצון העצמי שבבחינת מקיף דיחידה הנזכר לעיל, מאיר ובא בגלוי במוחין דחכמה ובינה, עד שיורד ומתצמצם בקטנות המוחין דכלי דנצח והוד דחסד מורגש שבלב, שהוא בהבל החזה
- הרי גם שם הרצון מאיר
phrases.en: Even there, the *ratzon* is still there; it's the same *ratzon*, even though it had to go through various *tzimtzumim*.

phrases.he: כי אנו רואים שבהבל הלב גם כן מורגש הרצון
phrases.en: So we see that even in the *hevel halev* the *ratzon* is *murgash*.

phrases.he: ונקרא רעותא דלבא,
phrases.en: It's called the *ratzon* of the heart.

phrases.he: מה שלבו חפץ במורגש לדבר טוב,
phrases.en: What his heart wants with actual feeling: not with intellect, and not even with the emotion, but the actual *hergesh* of it.

phrases.he: ולמאוס בהעדר הרצון בלב לדבר רע השנאוי כו'
phrases.en: Like for instance in fear, that he has a *hipuch haratzon* for this thing; he's trying to run away from it.

phrases.he: אם כן, מתאחד ומתקשר ממקור הרצון העצמי עד הבל הלב ברגע אחד,
כאילו הוא מהות אחד ממש
phrases.en: It's as if it's *mamash* one thing.

blocks.text: Even there the will shines, for we see that the will is felt in the breath of the heart: as he is getting mad, that comes from the will. Why is he getting mad? Because it goes against his will. And this inner will is called the *re'usa d'liba* (the will of the heart), what his heart wants.
blocks.outOfPlace: He reads ahead from line 38 into lines 40-42 here, until a listener tells him he skipped a few lines and he goes back.

blocks.text: As in the lower man: when the essential will of the encompassing *yechida* shines, revealed, in the brains of *chachma* and *bina*, and comes down and contracts into the small brains of the vessel of *netzach* and *hod* of the felt kindness in the heart, in the breath of the chest: **even there, the *ratzon* is still there; it's the same *ratzon***, though it had to go through various *tzimtzumim*, through the brain and the inner heart, all the way until he is breathing hard. The breathing shows there is a will.

blocks.title: The dog that wants food
blocks.text: You see it especially with a dog: when he wants some food, or wants something, he starts breathing hard.

**So we see that even in the *hevel halev* the *ratzon* is *murgash***: the will is felt in the breath of the heart. It is called **the *ratzon* of the heart**, what the heart wants with actual feeling, not with intellect and not even with emotion, but the actual *hergesh* (sensation): he feels that he wants this. And the opposite: in fear he has a *hipuch haratzon* (an aversion) to the thing and tries to run away from it, or if they tell him to work.
So the source of the essential will is united and bound to the breath of the heart in one moment, **as if it's *mamash* one thing**, as if the will is *mamash* in the heart.

phrases.he: והיינו דמיון להבין באדם העליון
phrases.en: And this is a *dimyon* to understand in the upper person.

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת זעיר אנפין
שבבחינת לב דזעיר אנפין נאמר ויאמר אל לבו, להטות לחסד
phrases.en: He told his heart *l'hatos l'chesed*, to be *noteh* towards *chesed*.

phrases.he: וכן ויתעצב אל לבו, לבחינת דין וכהאי גוונא
הרי בבחינת חיצוניות הכלי דנצח והוד דלב זה,
phrases.en: Meaning the actual feeling of the breathing of it.

phrases.he: מאיר שם מבחינת הרצון הפשוט העצמי שבעצמות אור אין סוף שלפני הצמצום הראשון
phrases.en: It's *mamash* the *ratzon*, the *ratzon atzmi*.

phrases.he: (הנזכר באות יו''ד בבחינת יחיד ואחד כו', במשל חפץ חסד העצמי בעצמות הנפש כו')
phrases.en: This is the *ratzon* which is talked about in chapter 10.

blocks.text: This is a likeness for the upper man, *Zeir Anpin*. Of its heart it says "And He said to His heart": **He told his heart *l'hatos l'chesed***, to lean toward kindness; and "He was saddened to His heart", toward judgement, at the flood. In the outer vessel of *netzach* and *hod* of that heart, **the actual feeling of the breathing of it**, shines the simple essential will from before the first *tzimtzum*. Though there is a change of essence, it makes no difference: **It's *mamash* the *ratzon***, the will spoken of in chapter 10.

phrases.he: ואם כן עד בחינת חיצוניות הלב דזעיר אנפין נחשב עדיין הכל מסוף עולם האין סוף
משום דאיהו וגרמוהי חד,
phrases.en: He is one, one with his organs.

phrases.he: כמו באדם,
phrases.en: Like a person, he's *mamash* literally one with his organs.

phrases.he: שלבו ורצונו העצמי אחד הוא כו' ודי למבין:
phrases.en: That his heart, meaning also his lungs, and his *etzem haratzon* is one thing, *mamash* one thing.

blocks.text: So even the outer heart of *Zeir Anpin* counts as the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*, brought farther and farther down. First even the *machshava kduma* (the primordial thought) was past it; then it was part of it, and *Adam Kadmon* only a new creation; then *Adam Kadmon* too was from it, and *Atik* and *Arich* a nothing that comes out of it; then the inner and outer *Atik*, then *chachma* and *bina*, then the inner heart. Now it reaches the *netzach* and *hod* of the outer vessels of *Zeir Anpin*, because it is completely connected, as a scared person's breathing changes automatically, with nothing in between.

Because "He and His causes are one": **He is one, one with his organs**, as a person is *mamash* literally one with his organs. His heart, meaning also his lungs, and his *etzem haratzon* (essential will) are one thing, *mamash* one thing. That is what is called the *gufa d'malka*.

So again, as in chapter 10: it is and it isn't. First he says it is not the *Ein Sof*: a *tzimtzum*, another *tzimtzum*, not even *chachma* and *bina*, then the narrow of the throat. So is it or isn't it? It depends what you are talking about. Is it the real *Atzmus* (Essence)? No more than a person's outer vessels, just flesh, are really him. From the other side, of course it is him.

reviewQuestions.question: How can the vessels of *Zeir Anpin*, down to the outer *Nehi*, still be the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*?
How do four brains of eight rooms make the 32 paths, and why do they give the heart its name?
What is the difference between the fifty gates of *bina* and the 32 paths, and what has *daas* to do with it?
Why must there be a withdrawal at the narrow of the throat before the mind's love becomes the heart's?
If the heart's *middos* come with a change of essence, how can they match the mind's exactly?
What does breathing hard when one is angry or afraid show about the will, and what does it teach about *Zeir Anpin*?

The whole tape continues the discussion of chapter 2 from the end of tape 050: the thought of Leah as letters, machshevas sechel as the meaning, and the analysis it holds (the gravestone cutter, the singer in fifty languages, the two washer ladies), up to the letters of Ana Emloch in Malchus of tevuna.

A listener brings a passage of chapter 2 (the parenthesis on Yisroel Saba and tevuna, Malchus of tevuna as machshevas sechel): the thought of Leah, machshevas sechel and machshava iyunis, with the word cat and "Row, row, row your boat". It continues on tape 051.

notes.text: Class 049: the alignment is right that it reads only line 28 (w1622-1647), and reads it without comment. Before it (w0-1621) it finishes the grid of brains and rooms from the end of class 048 (lines 16-27); after it, it stops the text (w1648-1719) and digresses on the 64 brains of one who contemplates and the sixty-fourth brain of pride (w1720-3232). Those blocks are under lines 25-27 with outOfPlace. The class's reading of line 28 is the second audio of the line-28 block.

Tape 051 (Tape36-Side1), listed with this chapter as reading no line, is entirely on chapter 2 (the parenthesis on Malchus of tevuna, machshevas sechel, the thought of Leah and machshava iyunis), continuing the end of tape 050 (w1959-4187). No block cites it; it is listed in omitted as other-chapter, and both stretches belong with chapter 2. The catalog's assignment of 051 to chapter 32 (and of 050's second half) is for the owner of data/classes.txt and chapter 2's guide.
Line 29: he reads "ריקון הגרון בשביל להשתנות ממאכל למאכל" (050 w37-45) for the printed רקבון הגרעין, "the rotting of the seed", and does not explain it; the block follows the line.
Line 30's English ("the tzimtzum between the brain and the heart ... the narrowness of the throat", 050 w75-96) comes after he has begun line 31 (w61-74); the phrases cite each where he says it.

Line 32: who says what in the exchange on the diaphragm and the liver (050 w113-375) is not clear; several voices speak. The block gives the conclusion: the diaphragm is a border, and the change is in the liver, a filter. The question is inferred from "A diaphragm?" (w130-131).

Line 20: the phrase's English ("the daas is mateh it towards these two brains of chesed and gevura") covers the whole line; he does not translate "כלפי זכות או כלפי חוב", but a cut there is not possible with the line's repeated words.
Line 4's first phrase is cut at the second סוף ("ועדיין הוא סוף עולם האין סוף"); its Hebrew was copied from the line by script, since "to" matches the first סוף.
048 w2504-2512: the word before "of goyishkeit" is transcribed תועלת and is unclear (perhaps to'eiva); the block says "the whole business of goyishkeit" and does not guess.

049 w2655-2721: he gives the saying on a Torah scholar's pride as "more than one sixty-fourth of gaava is called a gas ruach". The Gemara (Sotah 5a) has a scholar needing "an eighth of an eighth" of pride; the block keeps his wording.

049 w454-546: he first puts up as netzach and down as yesod, then corrects himself to up netzach, down hod, and himself yesod; the block has the final version. At w865-890 someone cites a text placing yesod in the west and Malchus in the middle ("in this תחילת חכמה"); the block says only "it says here".

047 w3567-3603: "when I learned this with her ... she's a doctor": the block says only "a doctor he learns with". 048 w293-349 names two students over a piece on screen colors; the block says "a student".
047 w3182-3237: a listener's question on two sets of 32 paths in Derech Chaim; he answers "It's the same one". The question is the student's as heard.
Line 48 reads הנזכר באות יו"ד; he reads "בפסוק" and says "chapter 10", which agrees with the line (the letter yud). His "כמשל כובד כעס" is a mishearing of חפץ חסד.
